Based on the search results, the highest-grossing film of all time is **"Avengers: Endgame"** (2019), which was directed by the **Russo Brothers (Anthony Russo and Joe Russo)**.

According to multiple box office sources, Avengers: Endgame grossed approximately **$2.94 billion worldwide**. Here are some key details:

- **Director:** Anthony Russo & Joe Russo
- **Release Year:** 2019
- **Worldwide Box Office:** ~$2.94 billion

The film briefly held the #1 spot over James Cameron's **Avatar** ($2.92 billion), which had been the previous record-holder for many years. While Avatar temporarily reclaimed the crown with a Chinese re-release in 2021, Avengers: Endgame regained the top position following another re-release in 2019 and subsequent box office tracking updates.

It's worth noting that box office rankings can shift due to:
- Re-releases in different countries
- Inflation-adjusted vs. nominal figures  
- Different accounting periods

James Cameron remains highly successful at the box office, directing multiple films that have ranked in the top tier (Avatar, Titanic, and Avatar: The Way of Water). However, according to traditional box office records, **Anthony and Joe Russo are the directors of the highest-grossing film ever made.**

CIThe Cinerama figures represent gross amounts. Since the Cinerama corporation owned the theaters there were no rental fees for the films, meaning the studio received 100% of the box-office gross, unlike the case with most other films where the distributor typically receives less than half the gross. Since Variety at the time ranked films by their U.S. and Canadian rental, they constructed a hypothetical rental figure for the Cinerama films to provide a basis for comparison to other films in their chart: in the case of This Is Cinerama, the $50 million worldwide gross was reconfigured as a $12.5 million U.S. rental gross; this is exactly 25% of the amount reported by Cinerama, so Variety's formula seemingly halved the gross to obtain an estimate for the U.S. share, and halved it again to simulate a rental fee.[67] All five Cinerama features collectively generated $120 million in worldwide box office receipts.[68]
GSVariety put the worldwide rental for The Greatest Show on Earth at around $18.35 million (with $12.8 million coming from the United States[58]) a year after its release; however, Birchard puts its earnings at just over $15 million up to 1962. It is likely that Birchard's figure is just the North American gross rental, and includes revenue from the 1954 and 1960 reissues.
SWThe "first run" Star Wars grosses do not include revenue from the 1997 special-edition releases; however, the figure does include revenue from the re-releases prior to the special editions.
HP1The Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone reissue totals recorded by Box Office Mojo for Brazil (2020), Italy (2021), Netherlands (2021) and South Korea (2021) have been deducted from the lifetime gross due to Box Office Mojo double-counting the original release grosses in those countries.
HP8Production costs were shared with Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 1.
Timeline of highest-grossing films  
The Birth of a Nation pioneered many of the techniques used in filmmaking today, becoming the most successful film ever made at the time of its release.

At least eleven films have held the record of 'highest-grossing film' since The Birth of a Nation assumed the top spot in 1915. Both The Birth of a Nation and Gone with the Wind spent twenty-five consecutive years apiece as the highest-grosser, with films directed by Steven Spielberg and James Cameron holding the record on three occasions each. Spielberg became the first director to break his own record when Jurassic Park overtook E.T., and Cameron emulated the feat when Avatar broke the record set by Titanic. When it took over the top spot in 2019, Avengers: Endgame became the first sequel to hold the record of highest-grossing film and, in doing so, interrupted thirty-six years of Spielberg/Cameron dominance. Since then, Avatar and Avengers: Endgame have traded the top spot on a couple more occasions, with Avatar reclaiming it two years later in 2021 following a re-release, and Avengers: Endgame doing likewise in 2026.
Some sources claim that The Big Parade superseded The Birth of a Nation as highest-grossing film, eventually being replaced by Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, which in turn was quickly usurped by Gone with the Wind.[69] Exact figures are not known for The Birth of a Nation, but contemporary records put its worldwide earnings at $5.2 million as of 1919.[70] Its international release was delayed by World War I, and it was not released in many foreign territories until the 1920s;

coupled with further re-releases in the United States, its $10 million earnings as reported by Variety in 1932 are consistent with the earlier figure.[71] At this time, Variety still had The Birth of a Nation ahead of The Big Parade ($6,400,000) on distributor rentals and—if its estimate is correct—Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs ($8,500,000)[72] would not have earned enough on its first theatrical run to take the record;[73] although it would have been the highest-grossing 'talkie',[74] displacing The Singing Fool ($5,900,000).[75] Although received wisdom holds that it is unlikely The Birth of a Nation was ever overtaken by a silent-era film,[76] the record would fall to 1925's Ben-Hur ($9,386,000) if The Birth of a Nation earned significantly less than its estimated gross.[77] In addition to its gross rental earnings through public exhibition, The Birth of a Nation played at a large number of private, club and organizational engagements which figures are unavailable for.[78] It was hugely popular with the Ku Klux Klan who used it to drive recruitment,[79] and at one point Variety estimated its total earnings to stand at around $50 million.[80] Despite later retracting the claim, the sum has been widely reported even though it has never been substantiated.[70] While it is generally accepted that Gone with the Wind took over the record of highest-grossing film on its initial release—which is true in terms of public exhibition—it is likely it did not overtake The Birth of a Nation in total revenue until a much later date, with it still being reported as the highest earner up until the 1960s.[78] Gone with the Wind itself may have been briefly overtaken by The Ten Commandments (1956), which closed at the end of 1960 with worldwide rentals of $58–60 million[81][82] compared to Gone with the Wind's $59 million;[83] if it did claim the top spot its tenure there was short-lived, since Gone with the Wind was re-released the following year and increased its earnings to $67 million.

Depending on how accurate the estimates are, the 1959 remake of Ben-Hur may also have captured the record from Gone with the Wind: as of the end of 1961 it had earned $47 million worldwide,[84] and by 1963 it was trailing Gone with the Wind by just $2 million with international takings of $65 million,[85] ultimately earning $66 million from its initial release.[86]
The 1972 pornographic film Deep Throat reportedly earned as much as $600 million, a figure that may have been inflated by gangsters in money-laundering schemes.
Another film purported to have been the highest-grosser is the 1972 pornographic film Deep Throat. In 1984, Linda Lovelace testified to a United States Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on juvenile justice that the film had earned $600 million;[87] this figure has been the subject of much speculation, since if it is accurate then the film would have made more money than Star Wars, and finished the 1970s as the highest-grossing film. The main argument against this figure is that it simply did not have a wide enough release to sustain the sort of sums that would be required for it to ultimately gross this amount.[88] Exact figures are not known, but testimony in a federal trial in 1976—about four years into the film's release—showed the film had grossed over $25 million.[89] Roger Ebert has reasoned it possibly did earn as much as $600 million on paper, since mobsters owned most of the adult movie theaters during this period and would launder income from drugs and prostitution through them, so probably inflated the box-office receipts for the film.[90]

After _Avengers: Endgame_ and _Avatar_ duked it out for bragging rights as the all-time highest-grossing movie in 2019, the world was hit by the COVID-19 pandemic, which effectively shuttered theaters (some of them never to reopen), and this list seemed safe for the time being. But in late 2021, _Spider-Man: No Way Home_ blew everyone away and nostalgia-bombed its way into the top 10.
Just a few months later, the decades-in-the-making sequel _Top Gun: Maverick_ also shocked the world by swooping past the $1 billion mark, and another half year later,_Avatar: The Way of Water_ proved James Cameron is the box office GOAT by shooting all the way up to the No. 3 spot. And with the addition of global hits _Inside Out 2_ in 2024 and _Zootopia 2_ in 2024, Disney now lays claim to a whopping eight of the top 10 highest-grossing films of all time (nine, if you count its joint ownership of _Titanic_ with Paramount).

# The 50 Highest-Grossing Movies of All Time: Your Top Box Office Earners Ever Worldwide
## 2026 has already given us three all-timers in _Toy Story 5_, _The Odyssey_, and _Spider-Man: Brand New Day_.
In 2023, _The Super Mario Bros. Movie_ surprised everyone by jolting into the top half of this list in just its first six weeks of release, ultimately landing at No. 16, and most were ready to call it a year. Then Barbenheimer fever hit, and before we knew it, we had a new champion that was not only the highest-grossing film ever solo-directed by a woman, but also the highest-grossing film in Warner Bros. studio history. 2025 was another big year, with three films — including James Cameron’s third _Avatar_ movie, _Fire and Ash_ — entering the top 20, and in 2026, after _Toy Story 5_ cracked the top 50, Christopher Nolan’s _The Odyssey_ and _Spider-Man: Brand New Day_ joined in quick succession, with the latter becoming the second-fastest film ever to reach the $1 billion milestone — it’s already sitting at No. 12 all time — and both still in theaters and climbing as of the latest update.
For the list below, we’ve included global box office performance, as well as domestic numbers and release dates. We included dollars earned in re-releases, and in each of our descriptions, we look at where the film stood record-wise at the time of its run and dive into things like critical and audience reception.**We’ll be here to track the progress of new blockbusters and regularly update this list of top box office performers. Directed By: James Cameron, Colin Wilson, Laeta Kalogridis
**Box Office: $2.924 billion worldwide / $785.2 million domestic (including re-releases)

The world had to wait some 12 years for James Cameron to follow up the biggest film of all time with what would become _the new biggest film of all time_. Nobody believed he was going to surpass _Titanic_’s numbers with this tale of an alien planet and the paraplegic Marine who teams up with its inhabitants in the battle for Unobtanium. But he did. At the peak of a 3-D reemergence, aided by the filmmaker’s usual technological gamesmanship (and higher ticket prices), **_Avatar_‘**s seven straight weekends at No. 1 led to over $595 million at the North American box office, ultimately becoming the highest domestic earner ever and the only film ever to earn $2 billion outside of the U.S. and Canada, making it the world’s highest grosser at the time. Nearly 10 years later, _Avengers: Endgame_ snatched the crown, but with an _Avatar_ sequel on the way in 2021, the now Disney-owned-and-rebranded 20th Century Studios decided to re-release the film in China and pushed it back into pole position.

## 2026 has already given us three all-timers in _Toy Story 5_, _The Odyssey_, and _Spider-Man: Brand New Day_.
As the journey that began in 2008 with _Iron Man_ was coming to an end, audiences who had been holding their breath after perhaps the biggest cliffhanger since _The Empire Strikes Back_ could not wait to buy their tickets— and did they ever _buy those tickets_ when they finally could. Opening weekend for _**Avengers: Endgame**_ in April 2019 surpassed _Infinity War_’s year-long record by nearly $100 million. In just eight days, the film had grossed a half billion domestically. One by one, the records fell, leading many to speculate when, not if, _Avatar_‘s previous record ($2.787 billion) would fall. But in the era of the modern blockbuster, even a record-breaker can be front-loaded and spend only three weeks atop the charts. After just six weeks of release,_Endgame_ was about$73 million away from dethroning _Avatar_ — substantial ground to make up. but Marvel and Disney re-released the film on June 28, 2019 with new goodies over its end credits. Over the weekend of July 19, 2019 — its 13th week of release — _Endgame_ squeaked ahead… at least for a while. With a 2021 re-release in China,_Avatar_ did ultimately take back the crown, but it doesn’t diminish the incredible achievement of _Endgame_.

## 2026 has already given us three all-timers in _Toy Story 5_, _The Odyssey_, and _Spider-Man: Brand New Day_.
**Box Office: $2.453 billion worldwide / $936.7 million domestic (through Sep. 17, 2026)
Release Date: July 31, 2026**
Before _Top Gun: Maverick_, _Spider-Man: No Way Home_ was a key catalyst in bringing audiences back to the movies. After living through 21 months of a pandemic, moviegoers returned in droves, giving it the second-highest opening of all time behind the MCU’s previous all-timer of a team-up, _Avengers: Endgame_. No one anticipated that _**Spider-Man: Brand New Day**_, minus multiple Spider-Men and his villains, could challenge those numbers. Then it swung in and took the all-time record with a $360 million opening weekend, just under $3 million more than _Endgame’_ s pre-pandemic haul in the summer of 2019. It took only seven days (the shortest ever) to reach half a billion domestic (_Endgame_ took eight and _No Way Home_ took 12). By the end of its second weekend, it was already in the top 10 of domestic releases ever, and it ultimately overtook _The Force Awakens’_ $935.6 million to become the highest domestic-grossing film of all time.

For 13 years, the arguments about whether or not James Cameron’s _Avatar_ maintained a cultural footprint strong enough to draw in the crowds again only increased. The counter-argument of “Don’t bet against the king” turned out to be the right one. Despite having just the 38th-highest opening weekend at the time, _**Avatar: The Way of Water**_ benefited around the world from word of mouth that another theatrical event was upon us. Spending seven weeks atop the box office (the same as its predecessor) and 15 in the top 10 (one more than the original), the sequel to the biggest film of all time erased all doubts. CIThe Cinerama figures represent gross amounts. Since the Cinerama corporation owned the theaters there were no rental fees for the films, meaning the studio received 100% of the box-office gross, unlike the case with most other films where the distributor typically receives less than half the gross. Since Variety at the time ranked films by their U.S. and Canadian rental, they constructed a hypothetical rental figure for the Cinerama films to provide a basis for comparison to other films in their chart: in the case of This Is Cinerama, the $50 million worldwide gross was reconfigured as a $12.5 million U.S. rental gross; this is exactly 25% of the amount reported by Cinerama, so Variety's formula seemingly halved the gross to obtain an estimate for the U.S. share, and halved it again to simulate a rental fee.[67] All five Cinerama features collectively generated $120 million in worldwide box office receipts.[68]

Timeline of highest-grossing films  
The Birth of a Nation pioneered many of the techniques used in filmmaking today, becoming the most successful film ever made at the time of its release.
texts.41:
At least eleven films have held the record of 'highest-grossing film' since The Birth of a Nation assumed the top spot in 1915. Both The Birth of a Nation and Gone with the Wind spent twenty-five consecutive years apiece as the highest-grosser, with films directed by Steven Spielberg and James Cameron holding the record on three occasions each. Spielberg became the first director to break his own record when Jurassic Park overtook E.T., and Cameron emulated the feat when Avatar broke the record set by Titanic. When it took over the top spot in 2019, Avengers: Endgame became the first sequel to hold the record of highest-grossing film and, in doing so, interrupted thirty-six years of Spielberg/Cameron dominance. Since then, Avatar and Avengers: Endgame have traded the top spot on a couple more occasions, with Avatar reclaiming it two years later in 2021 following a re-release, and Avengers: Endgame doing likewise in 2026.
Some sources claim that The Big Parade superseded The Birth of a Nation as highest-grossing film, eventually being replaced by Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, which in turn was quickly usurped by Gone with the Wind.[69] Exact figures are not known for The Birth of a Nation, but contemporary records put its worldwide earnings at $5.2 million as of 1919.[70] Its international release was delayed by World War I, and it was not released in many foreign territories until the 1920s;
texts.42: coupled with further re-releases in the United States, its $10 million earnings as reported by Variety in 1932 are consistent with the earlier figure.[71] At this time, Variety still had The Birth of a Nation ahead of The Big Parade ($6,400,000) on distributor rentals and—if its estimate is correct—Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs ($8,500,000)[72] would not have earned enough on its first theatrical run to take the record;[73] although it would have been the highest-grossing 'talkie',[74] displacing The Singing Fool ($5,900,000).[75] Although received wisdom holds that it is unlikely The Birth of a Nation was ever overtaken by a silent-era film,[76] the record would fall to 1925's Ben-Hur ($9,386,000) if The Birth of a Nation earned significantly less than its estimated gross.[77] In addition to its gross rental earnings through public exhibition, The Birth of a Nation played at a large number of private, club and organizational engagements which figures are unavailable for.[78] It was hugely popular with the Ku Klux Klan who used it to drive recruitment,[79] and at one point Variety estimated its total earnings to stand at around $50 million.[80] Despite later retracting the claim, the sum has been widely reported even though it has never been substantiated.[70] While it is generally accepted that Gone with the Wind took over the record of highest-grossing film on its initial release—which is true in terms of public exhibition—it is likely it did not overtake The Birth of a Nation in total revenue until a much later date, with it still being reported as the highest earner up until the 1960s.[78] Gone with the Wind itself may have been briefly overtaken by The Ten Commandments (1956), which closed at the end of 1960 with worldwide rentals of $58–60 million[81][82] compared to Gone with the Wind's $59 million;[83] if it did claim the top spot its tenure there was short-lived, since Gone with the Wind was re-released the following year and increased its earnings to $67 million.
texts.43:
Depending on how accurate the estimates are, the 1959 remake of Ben-Hur may also have captured the record from Gone with the Wind: as of the end of 1961 it had earned $47 million worldwide,[84] and by 1963 it was trailing Gone with the Wind by just $2 million with international takings of $65 million,[85] ultimately earning $66 million from its initial release.[86]
The 1972 pornographic film Deep Throat reportedly earned as much as $600 million, a figure that may have been inflated by gangsters in money-laundering schemes.
Another film purported to have been the highest-grosser is the 1972 pornographic film Deep Throat. In 1984, Linda Lovelace testified to a United States Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on juvenile justice that the film had earned $600 million;[87] this figure has been the subject of much speculation, since if it is accurate then the film would have made more money than Star Wars, and finished the 1970s as the highest-grossing film. The main argument against this figure is that it simply did not have a wide enough release to sustain the sort of sums that would be required for it to ultimately gross this amount.[88] Exact figures are not known, but testimony in a federal trial in 1976—about four years into the film's release—showed the film had grossed over $25 million.[89] Roger Ebert has reasoned it possibly did earn as much as $600 million on paper, since mobsters owned most of the adult movie theaters during this period and would launder income from drugs and prostitution through them, so probably inflated the box-office receipts for the film.[90]
